title: Line of Sight
subtitle: A survey of the Harrow chain
story:
Last spring a warning went up from Fenwatch and never reached the muster. The relief came late to a valley that had already burned, and the report filed afterwards blamed the depot, because the depot is where everything goes.

You are the warden of the Harrow chain. Your work is knowing which post can see which — a thing no ledger holds, because it was never anybody's paperwork.

The column marches at first light. You have the day on the ridge, the dispatch ledgers in your satchel, and a glass. Find out what actually broke.

done.title: The survey is written
done.body:
The survey is written, and it says what the last report would not. The march does not hang on its depot. It hangs on a gate fort with one hearth and the twentieth-largest post-bag of twenty, and if that gate had been watched last spring the warning would have come through.

You fold the ledgers away. The light has gone flat and white, and the cloud is on the tops.

escapeDone.title: The chain is lit
escapeDone.body:
Somewhere north of the gap the Kiln takes the light, and after that it is out of your hands. The column will not march blind.

You stay a while and watch it burn — four fires strung over the tops, holding above the fog like something moored. In the valleys below, nothing at all. The low road is gone, and it does not matter.
